Graph of the Predicted Effects of a Random Effect

Source: R/plot_random.R
plot_caterpillar.Rd

Selects the graph with one row for each level of the grouping factor of a modelterms7::random() term: the predicted effect with its confidence interval and, optionally, the unshrunk estimate of the level as an open circle. A term with several coefficients for each level, such as a random slope, gives one panel for each coefficient.

Usage

plot_caterpillar(
  raw = TRUE,
  sort = TRUE,
  level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  information = distributions7::expected_info(),
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

raw

Whether to draw the unshrunk estimates.

sort

Whether to order the levels by the predicted effect of the first coefficient.

level

The confidence level of the intervals.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the intervals.

information

An object from distributions7::expected_info() (the default) or distributions7::observed_info(), the weight of the working residuals.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotCaterpillar object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The predicted effect is the coefficient of the level, and the interval is \(\hat b \pm z_{(1+\text{level})/2}\,\sqrt{V_{jj}}\), where \(V\) is the variance matrix of the coefficients selected by vcov_type. The unshrunk estimate of a level is the least squares estimate of the coefficients of that level from the partial residuals \(Z_i \hat b_j + (z_i - \eta_i)\), over the observations of the level, where \(Z_i\) is the row of the design of the term, \(\hat b_j\) the predicted effect of the level, and \(z_i - \eta_i\) the working residual of the equation (see plot_effect()). With one coefficient for each level it is the mean of the partial residuals of the level, and for a gaussian random intercept it is the mean of the residuals of the level plus its predicted effect. A level with too few observations to estimate all its coefficients has no open circle.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_prior(), plot_random_cov(), plot_shrinkage()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(120), id = factor(sample(1:12, 120, TRUE)))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(12)[dd$id] + rnorm(120, sd = 0.5)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x + random(~ 1 | id), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(),
               dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "random(~1|id)", plot_type = plot_caterpillar())
